question.text: For 'Yamuna Infra AIF', invested capital after three drawdowns is INR 650 crore against a committed capital of INR 1,000 crore. What is the DRY POWDER / pending drawdowns at the fund level?

explanation.text: The Logic: Dry powder (pending drawdowns) = Committed - Invested = INR 1000 cr - INR 650 cr = INR 350 crore. This is the fund-level uncalled capital illustrated in Chapter 7 section on drawdowns. The Trap: Option B is invested capital. Option C is committed. Option D is additive error. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C commonly asks for the dry-powder identity — the 'undrawn' number is what LPs track against their cash plans. Manager's Pro-Tip: Track dry powder weekly against your deal pipeline. If dry powder > 12 months of realistic deployment, accelerate sourcing — LPs grow impatient with cash sitting idle and IRR decays.
